newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Iridium handphones to cost US$2,000-3,000.
newsitem.headline: Iridium handphones to cost US$2,000-3,000.

text.p: Global satellite mobile phone consortium Iridium said on Wednesday its new handphones would cost between US$2,000 and US$3,000 each.
Iridum LLC executive director for marketing Craig Bond told Reuters the consortium believed there was an addressable market for the phones of some 43 million users around the world.
He declined to give a sales prediction.

Iridium World Communications Ltd, which represents about an eight percent stake in the consortium, began trading in the United States on Tuesday and rose to $22-3/8 from the initial public offering price of $20.

Iridium is due to launch a global commercial phone network linking wireless telephones in September 1998, using 66 low-orbit satellites to deliver high quality communications to customers anywhere around the world.
